label: Tones
desc: The silent tone letter: pob, poj, pov, po, pos, pog, pom, and common words for each of the eight tone spellings

label: Consonants and vowels
desc: RPA letters English reads wrong (x, s, z, r, c, q, w), puffs of air (ph, th, kh), nasal starts (np, nt, nk), breathy nasals (hm, hn), and the vowels ee, oo, ia, ua

label: Greetings and courtesy
desc: Nyob zoo, ua tsaug, thov txim, sib ntsib dua: hello, thanks, sorry and goodbye the way Hmong Americans say them

label: About me
desc: I, you, he and she (and the "two of us" words), your name, where you are from, your clan, your languages, work and school

label: Family and kinship
desc: Parents, children, brothers and sisters (the word depends on who is speaking), grandparents, uncles, aunts and in-laws

label: Numbers and money
desc: Counting from one to a million, caug and caum for the tens, puas and pua for the hundreds, dollars and "how many?"

label: Things and classifiers
desc: Everyday things with their counting word: lub tsev, daim ntawv, rab riam, txoj hlua, phau ntawv, nkawm khau

label: Food and drink
desc: Rice, vegetables, meat, fish, eggs, noodles, chili, water, tea and coffee; noj for eating and haus for drinking

label: Time and days
desc: Today, yesterday, tomorrow, morning to night, days and months, clock hours, years, and every day

label: Feelings and weather
desc: Happy, sad, angry, lonely, scared, shy and tired; rain, wind, hot, cold and warm

label: Getting around
desc: Up there, down there, over there, inside, outside, left and right, near and far, cars, planes and roads

label: Shopping and money
desc: The market, prices, expensive and cheap, paying, buying, selling, discounts, and saying "more than"

label: Health and help
desc: Feeling sick, the doctor, the clinic and the pharmacy, fever and cough, medicine, appointments, interpreters, and asking for help

label: Talking with elders
desc: Greeting grandparents when they arrive and leave, "have you eaten?", respectful address, and the soft os

label: New Year and celebrations
desc: Noj peb caug: the ball toss, the qeej, paj ntaub, the silver sash, new clothes, songs, and happy birthday

label: Family events
desc: Clan, weddings and family gatherings, blessings and the wrist-string tie, and how families celebrate together

label: Questions and connectors
desc: What, who, where, when, how many, why, the puas and los questions, and the words for and, but, because and or

label: Traps for English speakers
desc: Tone twins (pob, pov, pog), the right counting word, no "is" before an adjective, peb or wb, and who says nus or kwv
